memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is what you are to do to consecrate them, so they may serve me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without defect. And from the finest wheat flour make round loaves without yeast, thick loaves without yeast and with olive oil mixed in, and thin loaves without yeast and brushed with olive oil. Put them in a basket and present them along with the bull and the two rams." - Exodus 29:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Aaron and his sons could serve as priests, something had to die. God lists the requirements: a young bull, two rams without defect, and loaves made from the finest flour. Consecration was not a ceremony of words alone. It cost something real, and it involved blood.

Notice the standard — animals "without defect," flour that was "the finest." God did not accept the leftovers or the second-rate for such a moment. What was offered to set apart His servants had to be the best available. This was serious, and the quality of the offering reflected the seriousness.

Being set apart for God has never been cheap. It cost Israel their best animals; it cost God His only Son. Peter reminds us that we were redeemed not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect (1 Pet 1:18-19). The very language of the ordination offering finds its fulfilment in Him. If you belong to God today, you were bought at a price. Never treat that lightly, and never imagine you were cheaply obtained.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I grasp the cost at which I was set apart for God?
Am I offering God my best, or what is left over?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I was set apart at enormous cost — the precious blood of Christ. Thank You for such a price paid on my behalf. Help me never treat Your grace as cheap. Amen.
